Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and heads up on Q4. I pulled together two pragmatic options that balance predictability for you and capacity planning on our side. See the attached draft (renewal-draft-v1.pdf) for line-by-line. Summary below.

Option A — 12-month price hold + burst pool
- 12-month rate lock on current SKU pricing
- 15% discount applied to committed volume if you renew at >= 100% of current commit (750k tokens/mo)
- Temporary burst pool available for Q4 at a predefined surge rate (40% premium over committed rate)
- Unused committed tokens convert to a quarterly credit bucket at list token rate (can be applied to overage or burst usage)

Option B — 24-month commit uplift
- 24-month term with a 22% discount on committed volume if you uplift baseline to 950k tokens/mo
- One-time bridging credit of $50k (applied as token credit) if you sign within 30 days
- Prorated true-up at year-end with rollover credits for unused monthly commit up to 20% of annualized commit

Operational notes:
- We can set up a burst pool governed by a usage cap and auto-fallback to the committed tier to avoid runaway spend.
- All credits are recorded as line-item offsets on monthly invoices; we'll provide an exportable credit ledger.

If procurement wants a spend-neutral starter, we can propose a short-term commit migration with a prorated credit to absorb peak demand while finance reviews the longer-term uplift.

Next steps: 30-min call? I can bring pricing and an SRE to talk about burst isolation and SLAs.

Best,
